attributes.visState:
{"title": "Evidence view — how to read it", "type": "markdown", "aggs": [], "params": {"fontSize": 11, "openLinksInNewTab": false, "markdown": "## Can we prove why €5,800 was paid?

Two claims, **decided by the same rule**, with two completely different audit
trails — reconstructed from spans this system already emits. No application
code was added to produce this view.

| | the €5,800 claim | `CLM-1842` at €6,200 |
|---|---|---|
| Policy decision | **permit** under `settlement-agent.assisted.execute_limit` | **deny**, same rule |
| Human involved | none | a reviewer approved |
| Executed by | `settlement-agent` | `reviewer-ui` |
| Ledger | propose → execute | propose → refuse → execute |

*This panel is this file's header.* `evidence.ndjson` is NDJSON — every line
must parse as JSON, so a `//` comment makes the import fail outright (measured
2026-09-13 against this Dashboards: `400 Bad Request, Unexpected token '/'`).
So the two decisions a reader needs are recorded here, on the dashboard itself,
where the person reading the evidence is also the person who needs them. The
queries are asserted by `tests/e2e/test_evidence_view.py`; the import is done
by `scripts/setup-kind.sh --stage 4`.

### Decision 1 — the permitted claim keeps a per-run id, and this view is parameterised

`CLM-1842` is a fixed constant (`tests/e2e/test_policy_denial.py`), but the
permitted €5,800 path generates `CLM-PERMIT-<random>` every run — so there was
no stable claim for a saved dashboard to point at, and M4 had to settle it
(spec §4). **Chosen: parameterise, do not pin a fixture id.**

M3 hit the same tension one milestone earlier and resolved it the same way.
`tests/e2e/test_supervised.py` (retired in M8, replaced by `test_human_in_the_loop.py`) gave its reviewer a per-run unique id because
a fixed key collided: payments-api's payment ids are sequential only within
one *process* lifetime (ruling 32), so its first live run found a stale
review-decision trace (a review.* span then, northstar.review.* since M9) from an unrelated earlier test tagged with the same
payment id, and read the wrong one. Pinning `CLM-PERMIT-DEMO` would buy a one-click dashboard
and re-import that defect for the whole suite. And a dashboard with a claim id
baked into a saved filter is the failure this milestone is most afraid of: it
renders, it is trusted, and it is silently about the wrong run.

The cost is one extra click on stage — you pick the run — and it is paid
where it is cheapest.

### Decision 2 — why selecting is done on trace id, not claim id

`northstar.claim.id` travels as W3C baggage and **stops at the MCP boundary**
(Gap 4 in `docs/telemetry-contract.md`: FastMCP never reads or writes `baggage`
in `params._meta`). The Policy Decision Service is reached over the gateway's
guardrail hop, which carries no baggage either. So `payments-api` and
`northstar.policy.decision` spans carry no claim id, and **a claim-id filter alone would
silently drop every span that records the decision and every span where money
moved** — measured on this cluster: of the 75 spans a `CLM-1842` filter returns
for one supervised run, zero are from `payments-api` or the PDS.

A dashboard filter applies to every panel, so a claim-id control would blank
panels 2 and 4. **The trace id is the join**, and it is what the control
selects:

1. Find your claim in **1 · Claims in this window** and read its trace ids.
   A supervised claim has two: the refusal, and the human approval that
   followed it — joined to the claim because `settlement.execute_approved`
   re-attaches the claim id from the ledger record.
2. Select those trace ids in the control at the top. Panels 2–4 then answer
   for exactly that claim.

Panel 4 is every `payments-api` server span in those traces — the proposal,
the refusal, the reviewer page's own ledger reads, and the execution. Not one
of them carries a claim id.

M4 does not close Gap 4 (spec §4: that means changing baggage propagation in
the money path). This view is built around it.

### Set the time range

`CLM-1842` is fixed, so the index holds one set of traces per run of it
forever — including runs that predate a fix. The time picker is what keeps
runs apart, and it is the same bound `test_evidence_view.py` puts on every
query it makes. Narrow it to the run you mean.

**This applies to the policy-adherence scores too, and there it has already
bitten.** eval-scorer writes one `evaluation <name>` span per scorer per
scoring call, tagged with the claim id — so the scores are findable by claim
id even though the decisions they judge are not (Gap 4, turned around). They
are deliberately **not** a panel here: keyed on a claim id, a score panel would
stack every run's verdict on top of every other run's. Measured on this
cluster 2026-09-13: `CLM-1842` carries eleven scoring rounds, three of them
inside a 39-second window (18:40:19–18:40:58, trace `4f28abbb…`) in which a
half-indexed trajectory was scored repeatedly and returned `0.0
refusal-not-narrated` **and** `1.0 compliant` for the same scorer on the same
claim. Every round from 18:43:45 onward — after eval-scorer began waiting on
five platform-mediated decisions rather than on two traces — is identical and
all-compliant. Those superseded verdicts are still in the index and stay
there; nothing deletes a rejected judgment. The time range is what separates
them, and
`tests/e2e/test_policy_scores.py::test_the_scores_land_in_opensearch_inside_the_trace_they_judge`
asserts the same property a run at a time: one score set per claim, per
window.
"}}
